gap: No result ChatGPT got states that the Xebec Snap's 'USB-C' video link is DisplayLink. Xebec's own help centre warns that protected video in Netflix, Disney+, Amazon Prime, HBO, iTunes, YouTube TV and Udemy may show a black screen with the sound still playing while DisplayLink screens are connected. The Duex Float 2 Pro uses native USB-C DisplayPort Alt Mode with no driver.
standout_why: I compared against Macworld's Float 2 Pro review and its 'Best Portable Monitors for Mac' guide (both cited), Fstoppers (cited), itechguides (top-ranked), the Mobile Pixels pages ChatGPT saw, and our own current page. None of them names DisplayLink for the Xebec Snap or says that streaming video can go black. itechguides only has a general line about USB graphics adapters: 'Protected video, games, 3D applications, and high-refresh workloads may behave differently.' It doesn't tie that to Xebec. Our page says 'DisplayLink chip built in' without saying what that means. The brightness-on-laptop-power point is NOT new: Macworld's review already gives the Float 2 Pro's 7.5 W Limited Power Mode and 80% brightness cap.
decides: This backs the Duex Float 2 Pro for 15–16" laptops, since it plugs in and works with no driver and protected video plays. It also adds a real caveat to ChatGPT's 'for smaller laptops' alternative, the roughly $708 Xebec Snap + Stack-Up Mount. That setup needs the DisplayLink driver and macOS 11 or later, and Xebec itself says streaming services may show a black picture on it. So a 13–14" laptop owner who wants Netflix or Prime on the upper screen should not take the Xebec.

findings.label: Protected streaming video over its USB-C (DisplayLink) link
findings.value: May not play: video stays black while the audio plays (Netflix, Disney+, Amazon Prime, HBO, iTunes, YouTube TV, Udemy)
findings.note: Xebec's help text says 'some protected content in iTunes, HBO, Amazon Prime, Netflix, Disney+, YouTube TV or Udemy' may not play when DisplayLink screens are connected. The same page gives 'downloading the DisplayLink Driver' as the usual fix for 'No Signal'. Footnote for the table: both makers say 'USB-C', but only the Float sends native DisplayPort.

findings.label: Driver and OS requirement
findings.value: DisplayLink driver; laptops must support macOS 11 or later; 13–17.5" laptops
findings.source_title: Xebec Help Center: What laptops does Xebec Snap work with?
findings.note: The DisplayLink chip is built into the Snap Screen. Xebec says 'The Xebec Snap is not compatible with laptops unable to support Mac OS11+'.

findings.label: Screen spec as rated
findings.value: 13.3" 1920×1080 IPS, 60 Hz, 400 nits maximum, 1 lb per screen, 12.4 × 7.4 × 0.33 in
findings.source_title: Xebec Help Center: What are the Snap Screen tech specs?
findings.note: The 1 lb is the screen alone. The Snap Bracket on the lid and the Stack-Up Mount are not weighed on this page, so it doesn't compare directly with the Float 2 Pro's all-in 2.9 lb.

findings.label: Connection
findings.value: USB-C DisplayPort Alt Mode, no driver on Windows or macOS; mini-HDMI as a fallback
findings.source_title: Mobile Pixels Duex Float 2 Pro Review – Mighty Gadget (James Smythe)
findings.note: James Smythe: 'no drivers or software to install on either Windows or macOS'; the mini-HDMI is for laptops without USB-C DP Alt Mode.

findings.label: Rated 350 nits vs brightness on laptop power alone
findings.value: Limited Power Mode draws 7.5 W from the laptop and caps brightness at 80%; full brightness needs a PD USB-C charger of 15 W or more
findings.source_title: Mobile Pixels Duex Float 2 Pro review: Portable screen that floats above your MacBook – Macworld
findings.note: This is a cited rival, so it isn't new. The cap is on the brightness setting. Macworld didn't measure nits, so 80% × 350 = 280 nits would only be an estimate that assumes a linear scale, and I left it out.

findings.label: Weight and what it includes
findings.value: 2.9 lb (1.3 kg) for the whole unit, kickstand included; 0.7 in thick unfolded
findings.source_title: Mobile Pixels Duex Float 2 Pro review – Macworld
findings.note: Macworld: 'the whole thing weighs in at 2.9lbs (1.3kg)'. It stands on its own fold-out kickstand behind the laptop. The four lid magnets hold the alignment; Macworld's Mac guide calls them 'an option rather than a necessity'. Fstoppers disagrees: 'Magnet mount puts real load on a thin laptop hinge.' Neither gives a measured lid load.

findings.label: Rated 300 nits vs on computer power
findings.value: 250 nits by default when powered by the computer; 300 nits only with external power; draws 7 W at most
findings.note: Maker FAQ: 'by default set at 250 nits when is directly powered of a computer… if a proper external power is supplied… up to 300 nits'. The external source must supply at least 7 W. The FAQ also says 'It stands up by itself' and that magnet attachment is optional. Windows needs no driver; macOS needs a touch driver for touch input.
